title: Fixtures as spun bodies (turning) or extruded profiles (vises): import from DXF or STEP, keep STEP as STEP

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Requested by the maintainer; sibling of #743 (tool and holder bodies as spun profiles).

## Two fixture variants
A fixture is one of:
- **Spun body** (turning: chucks, jaws, collets, faceplates): a half-profile on a centreline, revolved about the spindle axis. The same representation as #743's tool and holder bodies, and the same profile code.
- **Extruded profile** (milling: vises, jaws, parallels, step blocks): a closed 2D profile and an extrusion depth (along a chosen axis), placed in the setup.

## Import paths
- **From DXF.** A spun fixture is a centreline plus a half-profile, like #743. An extruded fixture is a closed profile plus the extrusion depth (entered on import, or from a DXF annotation/layer if present). Editable afterwards the way the half-profile is.
- **From STEP.** Imported as a solid and **kept and saved as STEP** in the fixture library (not converted to a profile): the fixture case keeps the vendor solid. A spun or extruded profile can optionally be derived from it, but the STEP stays the source.
- DXF read/write is shared with #743 (our own, from the published DXF reference: `LINE`, `ARC`, `LWPOLYLINE`, layers), with named refusals for unsupported entities and open or self-crossing profiles.

## Collision and simulation
- Spun and extruded fixtures are meshed for the fixture laws and the simulation from their exact profiles, so a profile edit changes what is checked and drawn.
- A STEP fixture keeps today's mesh path.

## Related
- #743: tool and holder bodies as spun profiles (shares the profile/DXF code).
- #339: handle fixtures and vises (umbrella); #561/#566 (locate the part in a fixture); the fixture library (`fixture_library`, #339); #723 (fixture_library test on Windows).

## Done means
- A spun fixture imports from a DXF half-profile and an extruded fixture from a DXF closed profile plus a depth. Both are tested: the meshed body matches the profile, and malformed input gives a named error, not a panic.
- A STEP fixture imports, saves to the fixture library as STEP, and re-inserts unchanged (test).
- The fixture laws and the simulation use the profile-built bodies (existing fixture suites pass; a new test checks a vise jaw built from a profile is hit by a rapid through it).
